# Documentation

How to keep documentation and in-code XML comments accurate and in sync with the code and the GitHub issue trackers.

- When adding, removing, or renaming public types, members, grain interfaces, or serialization aliases, update the relevant instruction sources in the same change: the public API type-name registry in `.github/skills/naming-conventions/SKILL.md`, the `Existing Primitives` / `Grain Key Conventions` tables in `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md`, and any affected prose in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
- Keep XML doc comments (`<summary>`) accurate - if you change a method's behavior, update its comment in the same commit.
- **Every `<see cref="...">` / `<seealso cref="...">` / `<paramref>` / `<typeparamref>` must resolve to a real symbol.** The packable libraries ship their generated XML docs inside the NuGet package (`GenerateDocumentationFile` is enabled for every project with a `PackageId` via `Directory.Build.targets`), so a dead cref is shipped to consumers and coding agents as a misleading dangling reference. When you add or edit a doc comment, keep its crefs valid: (1) use brace syntax for generic arguments, not angle brackets - write `cref="LwwValue{T}"`, `cref="IReadOnlyList{WalRecord}"`, never `cref="LwwValue<T>"`; (2) never put a nullable `?` inside a cref (`cref="Action{LatticeOptions}"`, not `Action{LatticeOptions}?`); (3) qualify a member or type that is not in the current file's scope with its declaring type or namespace (`cref="LatticeOptions.MaxLeafKeys"`, `cref="Orleans.Lattice.WalRecord"`); (4) for a method overload set, include the full parameter signature so the cref is unambiguous; and (5) for anything that is not a code symbol - a language keyword, a plain English word, or a type the project does not reference - use `<see langword="...">` or `<c>...</c>` instead of a `cref`. If you cannot confidently name a real target, prefer `<c>...</c>` plain text over a guessed cref. Verify by building the affected packable project with `dotnet build <csproj> -c Release -p:GenerateDocumentationFile=true -p:NoWarn=CS1591` and confirming it reports no `CS1574` / `CS1580` / `CS1584` warnings, and that its generated `bin/**/<Assembly>.xml` contains no `cref="!:` markers (the `!:` prefix is how the compiler records an unresolved cref). Note that `Directory.Build.targets` suppresses this cref-warning family for normal builds, so you must re-expose it with the `NoWarn=CS1591` override shown above to see the warnings.
- When adding a new primitive type, update the "Existing Primitives" table in `.github/instructions/primitives.instructions.md`.
- When adding a new grain, update the "Grain Key Conventions" table in `.github/instructions/grains.instructions.md` if it uses a structured key format.
- Topic-specific documentation lives under `docs/lattice/` (core library) and `docs/lattice.replication/` (replication package), mirroring the `src/` and `test/` folder layout. When adding a new document for the core library, place it in `docs/lattice/` and add a corresponding row to the **Documentation** table in `README.md`, keeping entries sorted alphabetically by document name.
- When changing behavior covered by an existing `docs/lattice/*.md` (or `docs/lattice.replication/*.md`) file, update that file in the same commit.
- **Every new metric instrument needs a dashboard panel and a map row.** When you add (or rename/remove) a `Counter` / `Histogram` / `ObservableGauge` / `UpDownCounter` on any of the `orleans.lattice*` `Meter`s (e.g. in `LatticeMetrics` / `LatticeReplicationMetrics`), in the same commit: (1) add or update a panel referencing the instrument in the matching bundled Grafana dashboard under `src/lattice.dashboards/Grafana/` (`OrleansLatticeReplication.json` for the replication meter, the core dashboard for the `orleans.lattice` meter) - the panel `expr` uses the Prometheus-mangled name (dots become underscores and a `counter` gains a `_total` suffix, e.g. `orleans.lattice.replication.doorbell.rung` becomes `orleans_lattice_replication_doorbell_rung_total`); (2) add a row to `docs/lattice.dashboards/metrics-to-panel-map.md`; and (3) document it in the relevant `docs/**/observability.md`. This is enforced by `DashboardJsonTests.Every_live_instrument_is_referenced_by_at_least_one_dashboard_panel`, which reflects over every live instrument and fails if any is unpaneled - so a new counter with no panel breaks the build. If an instrument is deliberately not charted, add it to `IntentionallyUnpaneledInstruments` in that test with a justifying comment instead.
- **Feature planning lives on [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/NSTA1/Orleans.Lattice/issues).** Each tracked feature, follow-up fix, or gap is a GitHub issue labelled `lattice` or `lattice.replication`. Reference work by issue number (e.g. #809) and by behaviour - describe the change by name and effect (e.g. "adaptive shard splitting" or "TTL on `SetAsync`") or link directly to the GitHub issue.
- **Dependency / sequencing information lives in the issue threads.** Use issue labels, milestones, and the issue body's "depends on #NNN" references to pick the next unblocked item; do not maintain dependency annotations in markdown.
- **All C# code snippets under `docs/` MUST use the `verify` fence attribute** (i.e. ```` ```csharp verify ````, not ```` ```csharp ````). The Roslyn-backed `DocsSnippetCompilationTests` harness recursively compiles every `csharp verify` fence under `docs/` against the real `Orleans.Lattice` surface, so the snippet must be self-contained and compile cleanly - declare any variables it references inline, or use the ambient identifiers the harness injects (`grainFactory`, `client`, `siloBuilder`, `tree`, `lattice`, `cancellationToken`, and the `User` / `Order` records). If a snippet is genuinely illustrative and cannot compile (e.g. pseudo-code or intentionally incomplete), convert it to plain prose or a non-`csharp` fence rather than dropping the `verify` marker.
